articles.title: Microsoft CEO Says 'Streamlining' at Xbox is 'Great to See' as Layoffs Affect Thousands
articles.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has spoken about the state of Xbox following layoffs that affected thousands of workers, saying that the "streamlining" at the company is "great to see." The tech executive opened up about how the business' gaming branch is doing during a recent interview on the Sources…
body: When touching on Xbox's place under the grander Microsoft umbrella, Nadella said he feels "fantastic" about the IP the brand has in its portfolio and its "ability to take that and produce great games going forward." As layoffs continue to reshape the developers who have made some of those great games, he still seems to be feeling pretty good.

"There's a certain amount of streamlining the team is doing and [Xbox CEO Asha Sharma] is doing, which is great to see," Nadella said in the wake of the most recent cuts. "And then, we have to invent the right sustainable business model that allows us to deliver gaming to more and more people.

"That has always been the goal, which is, we want to be a great publisher and a great platform provider for games across both PCs and Xboxes. So, that is our goal, and I think Asha and team have said that Xbox is going to get back to growth this next fiscal year, and that's the plan they're executing on, and in that process, do a bang-up job of producing some great games."
points: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has spoken about the state of Xbox following layoffs that affected thousands of workers, saying that the "streamlining" at the company is "great to see.

articles.title: Discord Users are Massacring Wumpus in Increasingly Gruesome Ways to Protest Platform's Age Verification System
articles.summary: Discord artists are tearing the company's purple mascot, Wumpus, limb from limb in increasingly gruesome ways to protest its controversial age verification system. Despite the backlash already surrounding Discord's new system, its launch started innocently enough.
body: "When you launch an extremely popular age assurance update that everyone on Discord was really looking forward to and it has bugs," Discord said.

The post in question was posted earlier this week and has 36K likes, but the nearly 10K replies already signal that not all is well amongst users. Open up the quotes for the post, and you'll be met with what feels like an endless sea of fan art featuring none other than Discord's plum mascot, Wumpus. These days, he's looking more red than purple, though.

The top post quoting the original message is accompanied by no text. Instead, it features a hyper-realistic version of Wumpus being subjected to a form of torture called "quartering," which sees an individual pulled into pieces by horses tied to each of their limbs.
This post alone has 260K likes. It is far from the only image of its kind.
points: Discord artists are tearing the company's purple mascot, Wumpus, limb from limb in increasingly gruesome ways to protest its controversial age verification system.

articles.title: Minecraft Is Getting Its First New Dimension In Over 15 Years
articles.summary: Announced today during Minecraft Live, Mojang is adding the first new dimension to the blocky sandbox game in more than a decade and a half. The Sift is an ethereal-looking fourth dimension that was first marketed for Minecraft Dungeons 2, and it's now been confirmed that it's coming to the base…
body: The Sift is a major new addition for Minecraft, marking the first new dimension since 2011's The End, where players go to fight the Ender Dragon in the end game. Speaking to GameSpot, Minecraft Dungeons 2 creative director Mans Olson explained that the team wanted to make sure that The Sift felt distinct from the Nether and The End rather than becoming another hostile environment.
"We wanted to make sure that it was different. That it doesn't feel like the ones that already exist in the game," he confirmed.

Unlike the Nether and The End, where the environments feel immediately hostile thanks to dangerous environmental hazards and angry mobs, the developers wanted it to feel like somewhere players could potentially live.
That doesn't mean that The Sift will necessarily always be completely safe. In Minecraft Dungeons 2, the dimension is under threat from the Illagers, leaving its ecosystem in danger.

articles.title: Everything Coming to Peacock in October
articles.summary: Peacock is going all-in on horror this month. A ton of scary movies are getting added to the service starting on October 1, including major franchises like Scream and Friday the 13th. Speaking of Friday the 13th, Peacock is also dropping a new original prequel called Crystal Lake on October 15.
body: If you're wondering what's worth watching, we've gathered together some of our top picks right here. You can also jump to all of the new releases for October for the full list by day.

Although Marvel's upcoming Blade movie has been tragically cancelled, the original trilogy is still ripe for the watching. After Wesley Snipes' cameo in Deadpool & Wolverine, the films have been harder to find. The trilogy being added to streaming service is worthy of a movie marathon celebration, especially during the spooky season. The second Blade is arguably one of the best vampire movies ever made after all.

Although The Mummy isn't the scariest of movies, it's still worth a rewatch in October. This is arguably the best Brendan Fraser movies of all time and the franchise is set to get its fourth installment in October 2027. Fraser has been reportedly training for the upcoming movie, which is bringing back many of the original characters that made it such a timeless classic.

articles.title: The Last of Us Gets Animated Background on PS5 as Naughty Dog Teases Announcements for TLOU Day 2026
articles.summary: Naughty Dog has released a free background on PlayStation 5 as it prepares to celebrate The Last of Us Day 2026. The studio behind Sony's exclusive post-apocalyptic video game franchise took to social media to tease some of what it has planned for this year's festivities.
body: PS5 owners can now head to their consoles to download a special The Last of Us-themed background for PlayStation's Welcome Hub landing page. It's a free option featuring both the younger and older versions of Ellie from both mainline games, with no download required to enjoy it. Although it's far from the kind of dynamic themes or wallpapers fans have begged Sony to bring back, the animated background does add some flavor for fans still hoping to see the series get a proper return in games.

Those who want to spice up their PS5 backgrounds need only to navigate to the Welcome Hub, select the Change Background button in the top corner of the screen, and then select The Last of Us background in the Games tab. It's nothing much, but we'll only have to wait a few more days to hear more about The Last of Us Day celebration.

In a separate post, Naughty Dog promised September 28 will bring even more reveals for the franchise. While it doesn't sound like something like The Last of Us Part 3 will be discussed, the team did promise to share a "partnership announcement, a very cool collaboration, digital surprises, and more." There will also be a No Return charity stream on Twitch.

articles.title: The Next Minecraft Update Adds Ice Caves, A New Mob, And More
articles.summary: Minecraft's next game drop will add a new underground environment to the sandbox game, along with a new hostile mob, and items that bring frosty mechanics to exploration and combat.
body: Announced during Minecraft Live on September 26, the upcoming game drop is expected to follow the usual drop cadence of once per quarter, releasing in December 2026. Its biggest addition is ice caves--a rare underground extension of Minecraft's existing cold biomes.

Ice caves will add more environmental variety to cold areas, giving you another reason to venture underground when exploring snowy regions. The caves will also contain ice crystals, which can be collected and used for decoration. Ice crystals can be placed vertically or horizontally, and they'll also produce light, giving you another way to illuminate your creations.

However, ice caves aren't entirely peaceful. A new hostile mob in the form of the Frozen Zombie will lurk underground, bringing new combat mechanics with it. Frozen Zombies can apply a stacking freezing effect with their melee attacks. If you take too many hits you'll eventually freeze, making getting surrounded by Frozen Zombies especially dangerous. They can also throw ice balls, which deal damage and knock players back.
points: Minecraft's next game drop will add a new underground environment to the sandbox game, along with a new hostile mob, and items that bring frosty mechanics to exploration and combat.

articles.title: Former D&D Leads Say Critical Role's Daggerheart Represents a ‘Fundamental Shift’ for TTRPGS
articles.summary: Chris Perkins and Jeremy Crawford are responsible for a lot of what Dungeons & Dragons looks like today. As two of the lead designers for the 5th edition of the game, they, along with Mike Mearls and many others, shaped much of D&D’s modern look, work that later carried on into the game's 5.5…
body: The two worked not only on the core rulebooks for both 5e and 5.5e, but also authored some of the most iconic and successful adventures published in the past decade, including Curse of Strahd, the best-selling D&D adventure of all time.

I can only imagine, then, how challenging it must have been for Perkins and Crawford to step into uncharted territory when, in 2025, they both joined Critical Role’s publishing arm, Darrington Press, to work on Daggerheart, a game whose rules they didn't design.

“For me, it was super easy,” Perkins says in a video interview with Polygon. “Even working on D&D, we were building on the work of previous editions and the labors of the people who made those additions. It's not like we were creating a game out of nothing.”

“For me, it's actually been a delight,” Crawford adds. “ Daggerheart is such a fun system to not only play in, but to work on. It has enough flexible parts to take and use to build new things, but it is also a new enough system that there's actually a lot of design space that we're exploring for future products.”

articles.title: 5 Nintendo Games That Still Need a Switch 2 Edition
articles.summary: The Nintendo Switch 2 is already on one heck of a run. Though it has yet to see new installments of some heavy-hitter franchises, Nintendo’s latest console has built up an impressive library of games over its first year and a half.
body: Though Nintendo has upgraded a fair amount of the Switch’s crown jewels so far, there are still a few games begging for the Edition treatment. That includes some top-tier games that could benefit from a tech boost and more niche ones that feel built for the Switch 2’s mouse controls. If there are any more Switch 2 Editions left in the tank, we hope that these make the cut.

Following the release of the Switch 2’s excellent Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, a Three Houses boost feels like a no-brainer. The tactics game brought the series to new heights of popularity in 2019 and gave the Switch one of its finest RPGs. It could use a visual and performance boost to bring it more in line with Fortune’s Weave as a treat, but that’s not the main draw. It would be a great excuse to bundle in all the content featured in its Expansion Pass, including its Cindered Shadows DLC. Heck, toss in a few alternate Fortune’s Weave costumes for characters like Seteth who appear in both games as a bonus.
points: The Nintendo Switch 2 is already on one heck of a run.

articles.title: Microsoft CEO says Xbox's "streamlining" is "great to see" despite cuts and layoffs
articles.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has praised Xbox's ongoing "streamlining" under Xbox CEO Asha Sharma just days after another round of layoffs hit the division.
body: Speaking on the Sources podcast with Alex Heath, Nadella was asked about Xbox's ongoing overhaul and the state of the brand and said he felt "fantastic".

"I feel fantastic about the IP we have right now," Nadella said (as transcribed by IG ). "If I look at the studios, the IP portfolio we have, and our ability to then take that and produce great games going forward - I feel fantastic. There's some amount of streamlining the team is doing, and Asha is doing, which is great to see."

He continued: "And then we have to invent the right sustainable business model that allows us to deliver gaming to more and more people. That has always been the goal, which is we want to be a great publisher and a great platform provider for games across both PCs and Xboxes.

"So that is sort of our goal, and I think Asha and the team have said that Xbox is going to get back to growth this next fiscal year, and that's the plan they're executing on, and in that process, do a bang-up job of producing some great games."

articles.title: 10 Years Later, Critical Role’S Most Heartbreaking Quote Still Lives in My Mind Rent-Free
articles.summary: It would be naive to expect zero changes when adapting something as expansive as Critical Role ’s actual play Dungeons & Dragons campaigns. The series has over 100 episodes, and each can run between 2 and 4 hours.
body: However, the changes for The Legend of Vox Machina started from the beginning, causing a ripple effect that ultimately led to one particularly heartbreaking quote from Campaign 1: Vox Machina hitting very differently within the constraints of its animated adaptation.

Scanlan lists all the times the party has sacrificed for one another — battling giants for Grog, going to the Hells for Pike, etc. — but not for him. When some of the party begin to protest, Scanlan’s question and later demand that they tell him his mother’s name (Juniper, if you’re curious) is so scathing the party can do nothing but fall silent. After all Vox Machina has been through, Scanlan uses his mother’s name — and the party’s ignorance of it — as further proof that they don’t really know or respect him.

What’s particularly memorable is that this quote marks the first time in Campaign 1 that Riegel raises his voice in anger at Vox Machina. Riegel often played Scanlan as exasperated, but here he reveals a man who realizes his choices have made his relationships feel transactional or skin-deep. It’s little wonder that Scanlan chooses to leave to work on his relationship with Kaylie.

articles.title: Minecraft Is Getting Its First New Dimension Since 2011
articles.summary: In the wake of layoffs and studio reshuffling at Xbox earlier this week, Mojang held a Minecraft Live showcase to make several Minecraft -related announcements. While we didn't get a look at the next movie, Mojang revealed a game-changing addition to Minecraft.
body: Mojang gave us a first look at the Sift at Minecraft Live and confirmed it will be added to Minecraft Java Edition and Minecraft Bedrock Edition in 2027. Before then, the Sift will play an important role in Minecraft Dungeons 2, a Diablo-like action-RPG spin-off set to launch on Sept. 29. From Minecraft Dungeons 2 's segment of Minecraft Live, we can tell the Sift is an ethereal, spirit-world-like dimension.

Currently, Minecraft consists of three fairly ubiquitous dimensions: the Overworld, the Nether, and the End. By the time the game exited its public alpha and beta testing in Nov. 2011, all three of those dimensions were part of the game. In the nearly 15 years since, Mojang has simply expanded the content available in those dimensions rather than adding any new ones. That'll finally change next year.

While that's certainly the highest-profile announcement from this Minecraft Live, the reveals didn't stop there. Mojang showed how the next game drop will add ice caves as a new underground biome. In ice caves, players can fight the new Frozen Zombie mob, equip and craft the ice balls those enemies fight with, and mine ice crystals.

articles.title: Former Elder Scrolls designer Kurt Kuhlmann on Fallout: New Vegas diehards: 'I don't know that Todd wanted to create that situation again for The Elder Scrolls'
articles.summary: I want to establish my old school RPG sicko bona fides really quick: My favorite Fallout games are 1 and New Vegas. My least favorite is 3 (4 is better than it gets credit for in critical circles). I really did not like Starfield and did not make it past the first planet.
body: With that out of the way, it is deranged how a lot of fans talk online about Bethesda as a studio, and Todd Howard as a guy. I have no doubt as to the accuracy of Kuhlmann's assessment of his former boss.

And I don't blame Howard one bit for being protective of the series in this way⁠. It's pretty relatable, and I'm sure it wasn't the only consideration around avoiding mainline-style spinoffs, as Kuhlmann's thoughts on ESO indicate.

Reading this in bad faith, you could parse it as an admission of weakness or insecurity, but I don't see it that way. I've spoken to senior Bethesda devs myself and watched them in other interviews: They're proud of their own work, speak positively of New Vegas, and seem to respect their peers at Obsidian. I think it's YouTubers impugning their character or calling for their coworkers to be fired over a perceived mishandling of the series that gets on their nerves.

Fallout memers seem to have gotten what they wanted, but in a monkey's paw kind of way. Obsidian is making a new Fallout game now, but with a gun to its head. Given all the layoffs and studio closures Xbox has under its belt, with more no doubt on the way, it doesn't feel like anybody's winning.
points: I want to establish my old school RPG sicko bona fides really quick: My favorite Fallout games are 1 and New Vegas.
My least favorite is 3 (4 is better than it gets credit for in critical circles).
I really did not like Starfield and did not make it past the first planet.
With that out of the way, it is deranged how a lot of fans talk online about Bethesda as a studio, and Todd Howard as a guy.
articles.author: Ted Litchfield

articles.title: Castlevania celebrates turning 40 by giving away the original game for free
articles.summary: In celebration of the 40th(!!) anniversary of Castlevania, Konami is giving away the original 1986 game for free on the App Store and Google Play.
body: The original Castlevania, which first released on the original NES in 1986, will be free to download until 24th October 2026, and other games across the series are available with deep discounts as we brace ourselves for the next entry, Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, next month.

The original Castlevania introduced vampire hunter Simon Belmont and his fight against Dracula while the new mainline entry, Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, follows the daughter of Castlevania 3's Trevor Belmont, Rose, as she fights her way through Paris and Dracula's castle with the Vampire Killer whip in 1499. It's slated to release on 15th October for Nintendo Switch, PC via Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

Alongside that, a series-wide sale is running across two storefronts. On the PlayStation Store, the Castlevania Anniversary Collection is 80 percent off from now until 7th October, the Dominus Collection is 50 percent off, and the Advance Collection and the Requiem: Symphony of the Night & Rondo of Blood bundle are both 70 percent off.
points: In celebration of the 40th(!!) anniversary of Castlevania, Konami is giving away the original 1986 game for free on the App Store and Google Play.

articles.title: MobyGames video game database now lets developers claim their game credits
articles.summary: Video game database MobyGames will let developers claim video game credits and customise their personal portfolios, albeit only via a new premium tier.
body: As reported by our sister site GamesIndustry.biz, MobyGames Professional launched in beta in June, with a full 1.0 version due this autumn. Alongside enabling developers to claim credits of games they've worked on via a verification process, it also lets users build a personal portfolio page on the site.

Talking specifically about the verification process behind claiming a page, which stops short of letting anyone edit their actual credit listings, Denzel said: "There's two parts to that. One is making sure that people are who they say they are, and that's a human-driven verification process that we run in the background. When it comes to making sure that credit history is reflected appropriately, the actual way that we do credits and credit verifications has not changed: It's not changed since Atari has been involved, it's not changed in a long time, and we have no plans to change that process". Atari acquired MobyGames in March 2022.
points: Video game database MobyGames will let developers claim video game credits and customise their personal portfolios, albeit only via a new premium tier.

articles.title: TALON TOWERS is a Fumito Ueda-coded parkour platformer about hopping around massive structures while avoiding falling to your foggy doom
articles.summary: If your game immediately makes me think of any of Fumito Ueda's in any sort of way, the likelihood is that I am to play it. There are only so many Ueda games (three, by my count) and there will only be so many (hopefully more that upcoming fourth one isn't the last), so when something rocks up that…
body: TALON TOWERS is the next game from Jan Malitschek, the dev behind brutalist first-person climbing platformer BETON BRUTAL, this time getting some help from Blanksword's Quinn K. and If Found's Hyphinett. The Uedaness of it all comes from the setting, these towers look old, as if there's a storied history to them. A history, I might add, that perplexes as much as it impresses; why are there so many criss-crossing parts to parkour across? I don't know the answer, but I'm not fussed about it because the platforming looks grand.

You've got a lot of movement tools at your disposal. You can run, climb, swing across monkeybars, wallrun and -kick, walk across tightropes, crouch and crawl, it looks incredibly expressive and tricky to get a handle on. A lot of those platforms are mighty narrow, and the way down looks… well, I don't know, there could be a bunch of pillows down there, but I assume it's not great. You can check all of it above in a nice and lengthy showcase for a game that only just got announced.
